scenarios.name: last-customer-typed
scenarios.why: the operator types LGSE 0000000050: RECEIVE gives 15 bytes, the 10 after the transaction id go into LastCustNum; DELETEQ TS GENAERRS / GENASTRT / GENASTAT / GENACNTL (GENASTAT is not there: QIDERR, caught by RESP); WRITEQ TS GENACNTL '**** GENAPP CNTL'; the second WRITEQ (FROM WRITE-MSG-L X(13) LENGTH(23)) is past its FROM item: X6, written padded, the task compared on

scenarios.name: transaction-id-only
scenarios.why: LGSE alone: RECEIVE gives 4 bytes (not > 5), LastCustNum keeps its VALUE 11; the four DELETEQs (none there: QIDERR each), the first WRITEQ, then the second, past its FROM item (X6, written padded)

notes: GenApp's setup transaction (LGSETUP, transaction LGSE in base/cntl/cdef121.jcl, a terminal transaction). It RECEIVEs the operator's line (an unformatted RECEIVE: the scenario's terminal input; STARTCODE 'TD') and, when more than the transaction id was typed, takes the last customer number from it; deletes TS queues GENAERRS, GENASTRT, GENASTAT and GENACNTL; writes GENACNTL's three items ('**** GENAPP CNTL', 'LOW CUSTOMER=...', 'HIGH CUSTOMER=...'); deletes and defines the named counters of pool GENA (GENACUSTNUM at the last customer number, the 48 statistics counters at 0); SEND TEXT FROM(WRITE-MSG-H) LENGTH(24); RETURN. The second WRITEQ writes FROM(WRITE-MSG-L), PIC X(13), LENGTH(23) -- ten bytes past its FROM item, which CICS copies from whatever follows in storage, a layout no oracle here can say; since #6573 it is written padded (FROM's bytes then spaces; oracle_assumptions.md X6, ASSUMED on both sides, not settled on z/OS, #4050), so the task runs on and is compared whole (DELETEQ TS is not an event on either side; it shows only in what a later READQ reads). Not proven: the SEND TEXT FROM(WRITE-MSG-H) LENGTH(24) also runs past its FROM item and the det port holds the PIC 9(10) after it as a typed number that never reaches the record's bytes, so Java sends HIGH CUSTOMER=0000000000 where GnuCOBOL sends the customer number (baselined in det_sweep_baseline.json, #5252).
